units.title: Embeddings, positions and the vocabulary axis
outcomes: Explain embedding lookup with a [V, D] table and trace [B, T] token IDs to [B, T, D] vectors.
Distinguish learned absolute positions, fixed sinusoidal positions and relative-position schemes.
Explain why computing an encoding beyond the training length does not prove useful length extrapolation.
units.why: Token IDs select rows; their numerical order carries no meaning. Position representations supply information that a token lookup alone cannot provide.

next.note: Project the token vectors into queries, keys and values.
Put relative-position structure into attention scores.

study.title: Absolute and sinusoidal positions
study.locator: Sections 1 to 3, then Appendix: Extrapolation of Sinusoidal Position Encoding
study.depth: Read the relative-position vocabulary in the appendix; leave interpolation and long-context methods for later.

focus: The vocabulary axis indexes rows. A [B, T] integer tensor gathers vectors without allocating a [B, T, V] one-hot tensor.
Repeated IDs select identical vectors before position information or contextual layers are applied.
Learned and sinusoidal encodings are absolute-position representations. RoPE changes Q and K rather than adding a position vector to the input.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, draw a [3, 2] embedding table, gather IDs [2, 0, 2], and add distinct position vectors. Explain which two vectors match before the addition and why they need not match afterward.
traps: Treating adjacent token IDs as similar numbers. IDs are labels, not coordinates.
Calling sinusoidal encoding a guarantee of long-context accuracy. Its formula extends; the learned model's behavior may not.

selfTest.q: With V=1000, D=32 and IDs shaped [2, 5], what are the table and output shapes?
selfTest.a: The table is [1000, 32], the output is [2, 5, 32], and the table has 32,000 parameters.

selfTest.q: Does moving a token to another position change its raw lookup vector?
selfTest.a: No. The same ID selects the same row. Position addition or later contextual processing can change its representation.

selfTest.q: Is sinusoidal encoding relative just because it can express offsets?
selfTest.a: No. It assigns a vector to each absolute position. Trigonometric identities let fixed offsets relate those vectors; RoPE instead writes a relative rotation into Q-K dot products.

Diagnose scale, mask-polarity and fully masked-row failures using a small explicit reference.
units.why: Attention is a weighted read from permitted keys, not a framework black box. Correct shapes and masks make the decoder's causal information boundary testable.

next.note: Batch this operation across independent heads.

study.locator: Equivalent Python implementation, boolean-mask semantics note, and Parameters: attn_mask and is_causal
study.depth: Read this after your explicit oracle works. Use the contract for padding-mask broadcasting; skip kernel selection.

focus: For X=[B, T, D], Q and K are [B, T, d_k], V is [B, T, d_v], scores are [B, T, T], and the output is [B, T, d_v].
With independent zero-mean unit-variance Q and K components, their dot product has variance d_k. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps the variance near one.
Subtract each score row's maximum before exponentiating. Mask forbidden entries before softmax and normalize over keys.
An allow mask combines j<=i with valid_key[b,j]. Broadcast key validity as [B, 1, T]; exclude padded query outputs separately and define a policy for rows with no valid key.
units.reproduce: From a blank file, compute one causal attention row with explicit dot products, max-subtracted exponentials and a weighted sum of V. Match it with a batched implementation on a three-token example containing a masked key.
traps: Using sqrt(D) after splitting into heads. The scale uses the query/key width of one head.
Copying a boolean mask between APIs without checking polarity. CS336 and SDPA use True for allowed entries; MultiheadAttention padding masks use True for blocked entries.
Assuming max subtraction fixes an all-negative-infinity row. It gives undefined subtraction; reject that row or explicitly return zero for an ignored padded query.

selfTest.q: If all allowed logits gain 1000, should the attention output change?
selfTest.a: No. Softmax is invariant to a common additive shift; max subtraction avoids overflow.

selfTest.q: Why does replacing a forbidden score with zero fail?
selfTest.a: exp(0) is one, so the forbidden key receives probability. Use negative infinity before softmax.

selfTest.q: Does a causal mask remove padding keys?
selfTest.a: No. It only forbids future positions. A padding key earlier than the query is still causally permitted and needs a separate validity mask.

selfTest.q: With Q=[2, 3, 4], K=[2, 5, 4] and V=[2, 5, 6], what are scores and output?
selfTest.a: Scores are [2, 3, 5], softmax runs over the five keys, and output is [2, 3, 6].

study.locator: Equivalent Python implementation, dropout warning, numerical backend note and Shape legend
study.depth: Compare only after the explicit per-head oracle passes. Set dropout_p=0.0; kernel tuning is outside this unit.

focus: With D=H*d, split [B, T, D] to [B, T, H, d], then transpose to [B, H, T, d]. A reshape alone does not exchange T and H.
Each head normalizes its own [T, T] score matrix. Concatenate head outputs before applying the output projection.
Reverse the transpose before merging. A transposed tensor may need contiguous storage or reshape rather than view.
Transfer identical weights into a per-head loop and the batched path. Backpropagate the same scalar contraction of outputs and compare gradients, not just shapes.
units.reproduce: Implement causal two-head attention for B=2, T=3, D=8. Reproduce its output and gradients with a loop over heads using sliced projection weights, then compare the attention core with SDPA at zero dropout.
traps: Comparing separately initialized modules. Different random weights do not test implementation equivalence.
Merging [B, H, T, d] directly into [B, T, D]. This silently scrambles head and token ordering.
Assuming eval() disables functional SDPA dropout. Its dropout_p argument must be zero explicitly.

selfTest.q: For B=2, T=5, D=12 and H=3, what shapes enter attention and leave the merge?
selfTest.a: Q, K and V are [2, 3, 5, 4], scores are [2, 3, 5, 5], and the merged output is [2, 5, 12].

selfTest.q: At fixed D, does doubling H double the bias-free MHA projection parameter count?
selfTest.a: No. Head width halves, so Q, K, V and output projections still total 4D^2 parameters.

selfTest.q: Why compare projection-weight gradients as well as input gradients?
selfTest.a: They check that each head uses and differentiates the intended weight slice. A forward-only or input-only comparison can miss a detached or incorrectly registered parameter.

study.title: Contiguous grouped-head reference
study.locator: Equivalent Python implementation: enable_gqa and repeat_interleave; GQA constraints note; Parameters and Shape legend
study.depth: Use the head mapping and functional contract after your explicit grouped oracle passes. Skip backend and kernel tuning.

focus: Let D=Hq*d and Hkv divide Hq. Q is [B, Hq, T, d]; unexpanded K and V are [B, Hkv, T, d]. MHA has Hkv=Hq; MQA has Hkv=1.
In PyTorch weight layout, Wq and Wo are [D, D], while Wk and Wv are [Hkv*d, D]. The bias-free total is 2D^2 + 2D*Hkv*d.
SDPA maps query head h to KV head floor(h/(Hq/Hkv)). The notebook's expand-then-reshape instead interleaves KV heads; choose one convention and make weight ordering and the oracle agree.
Optional comparison: allocate unexpanded K and V at the same B, T, d and dtype for MHA and GQA, then compare numel()*element_size(). Do not count expanded temporary tensors as compact cache storage.
units.reproduce: Implement a causal grouped-head loop and batched path for D=16, Hq=4 and Hkv=2, using contiguous groups. Derive 768 projection parameters versus MHA's 1024, and show that compact KV tensors use half the bytes at matched B, T and dtype.
traps: Using repeat rather than repeat_interleave while assuming contiguous groups. Shapes match, but queries read the wrong KV head.
Storing expanded K and V as the cache. That loses the compact representation's memory saving.
Expecting independently initialized MHA and GQA to produce equal outputs. Sharing restricts projections; equality needs a deliberately expanded shared-weight MHA reference.

selfTest.q: With Hq=8 and Hkv=2 under contiguous grouping, which query heads share KV head 1?
selfTest.a: Zero-based query heads 4, 5, 6 and 7. Each group contains Hq/Hkv=4 query heads.

selfTest.q: For D=1024, Hq=16 and Hkv=4, what are the K weight shape and total projection parameters?
selfTest.a: d=64, so Wk is [256, 1024]. The four bias-free projections total 2,621,440 parameters, versus MHA's 4,194,304.

selfTest.q: Does four times fewer KV heads imply four times less QK attention work?
selfTest.a: No. Every query head still computes scores and a weighted value sum. KV projection and compact storage costs shrink; the number of query-head score matrices stays the same.

selfTest.q: For B=1, T=2048, d=128 and two-byte elements, what does changing 32 KV heads to 4 save per layer?
selfTest.a: K plus V fall from 33,554,432 bytes to 4,194,304 bytes: 32 MiB to 4 MiB, an 87.5% reduction.

units.title: RoPE: positions as rotations

Implement RoPE on Q and K with explicit position IDs, head-local pairs and preserved output dtype.
Detect pairing and offset errors using norm, common-offset and nonzero-position tests.
units.why: RoPE makes position differences enter attention through rotations of Q and K. An implementation that silently restarts positions at zero can pass a short demo and fail incremental decoding.

next.note: Insert rotary attention into the pre-norm residual block.
Preserve absolute positions when appending rotated keys.

study.title: Explicit position IDs and rotary attention contract
study.locator: Section 3.4.3, Relative Positional Embeddings and problem (rope), printed pp. 22 to 23; section 3.4.5, Applying RoPE, printed p. 25

focus: For zero-based pair r, frequency is theta^(-2r/d). Rotate [x_2r, x_(2r+1)] by position*frequency using radians, not degrees.
R_i^T R_j=R_(j-i). The positional factor depends on the difference; content vectors q and k still matter.
Apply the rotation after projection and head splitting to Q and K, not V. Require an even rotary width and agree on adjacent-pair versus split-half layout.
Index sin/cos with the supplied positions, including nonzero offsets. Compute angles and rotations in float32 when needed and cast the result back; buffers are not trainable weights.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, multiply the two 2D rotation matrices to derive R_i^T R_j=R_(j-i), then implement adjacent-pair RoPE. For fixed q and k, verify equal dot products at positions (2, 5) and (12, 15) and compare against the unrotated relative-rotation expression.
traps: Mixing adjacent pairs with a split-half reference without permuting channels and projection weights. Both conventions can work, but their raw tensors are not interchangeable.
Using arange(T) instead of supplied position IDs. This discards offsets and per-sequence positions.
Inferring monotonic distance decay or reliable long-context quality from the identity. Rotations are periodic, and the identity alone guarantees neither.

selfTest.q: Why do a common offset c on query and key positions cancel?
selfTest.a: R_(i+c)^T R_(j+c)=R_(j-i), assuming unchanged q, k and frequencies. The rotary positional factor is unchanged.

selfTest.q: With theta=10000 and d=4, what frequencies do the two adjacent pairs use?
selfTest.a: 1 and 0.01 radians per position. Position p gives angles p and p/100.

selfTest.q: Should rotating a vector change its norm?
selfTest.a: Not in exact arithmetic. Each 2D rotation is orthogonal; numerical tests allow a dtype-appropriate tolerance.

selfTest.q: For a full paired rotation, what should happen with an odd head width?
selfTest.a: Reject it unless a separate partial-rotation contract explicitly leaves a channel unrotated. The assignment's full paired construction needs an even width.

study.title: Depth-scaled residual initialization
study.locator: MLP and Block classes; GPT.__init__ from self.apply(self._init_weights) through the c_proj.weight initialization loop; GPT._init_weights
study.depth: Use this as a contrasting GPT-2 recipe, not a replacement for the CS336 test architecture. Skip pretrained loading, optimizer setup and generation.

focus: Write y=x+Attn(RMSNorm(x)), then z=y+FFN(RMSNorm(y)). Normalize the branch input, not the residual sum; final stack normalization comes later.
LayerNorm subtracts the feature mean and divides by feature standard deviation. RMSNorm divides by sqrt(mean(x^2)+eps), without centering, and uses one learned gain per feature.
SwiGLU is W_down(SiLU(W_gate*x) * (W_up*x)). Its gate is not bounded to [0, 1]. Three bias-free matrices cost 3D*F parameters; a two-matrix GELU FFN costs 2D*F at the same hidden width.

CS336 specifies truncated-normal component weights and unit RMSNorm gains. nanoGPT instead uses base std=0.02 and residual-projection std=0.02/sqrt(2L); that scales initial branch weights, not the residual identity path.
units.reproduce: From a blank file, implement a pre-norm RMSNorm-SwiGLU block with the causal attention you already own. Zero the attention output projection and FFN down projection: the block must return x and give the identity input gradient, with dropout disabled.
traps: Normalizing across tokens instead of the feature axis. That couples positions and can leak future information even when attention is causal.
Squaring low-precision activations before upcasting. Overflow has already happened; accumulate RMS statistics in float32 first.
Copying the notebook's explanation that a SwiGLU gate is a probability. SiLU can be negative or exceed one; the sigmoid factor alone is bounded.

selfTest.q: For x=[1, 3, 5, 7], unit gains and negligible epsilon, how do LayerNorm and RMSNorm differ?
selfTest.a: LayerNorm gives [-3, -1, 1, 3]/sqrt(5), before any affine shift. RMSNorm gives [1, 3, 5, 7]/sqrt(21), whose mean is not zero.

selfTest.q: Why does SwiGLU often use F near 8D/3 instead of 4D?
selfTest.a: Three matrices give 3D*F weights. Setting F=8D/3 matches the 8D^2 weights of a two-matrix FFN with hidden width 4D, before rounding or biases.

selfTest.q: What is the clean gradient path supplied by x+f(norm(x))?
selfTest.a: Its Jacobian includes an identity term plus the branch Jacobian. Unlike post-norm, the residual identity contribution does not pass through a normalization Jacobian; this is not a guarantee against every training instability.

selfTest.q: In nanoGPT, why are both attention and MLP c_proj weights scaled with layer count?
selfTest.a: Both project branch outputs back into the residual stream. With two residual branches per layer, the recipe reduces their initial standard deviation by sqrt(2L) to limit accumulation across depth.

focus: One configuration owns V, D, layer count L, query and KV head counts, FFN width F, RoPE theta, context policy and tying. Validate divisibility before creating weights; different layers share a design, not all their parameters.

A tied head uses the same [V, D] Parameter as input lookup and computes h @ E^T. Equal initial values in separate Parameters are not tying; gradients from lookup and classification must accumulate into one weight.
For bias-free MHA with two RMSNorms and SwiGLU per block, untied parameters are 2VD + L*(4D^2 + 3DF + 2D) + D. Tying subtracts VD; standard RoPE adds no learned parameters.

List dense forward terms: per layer 8BTD^2 for MHA projections, 4BT^2D for QK and AV, and 6BTDF for SwiGLU matrices; the vocabulary head adds 2BTDV. Use the slow per-head oracle and suffix interventions to check causality, not a loss curve.
units.reproduce: Build a two-layer decoder with V=32, D=16, H=4 and F=48, using bias-free MHA, RoPE, two RMSNorms per block and one final RMSNorm. Derive 7,760 untied or 7,248 tied parameters, reconcile with unique registered weights, and verify unchanged prefix logits after replacing every suffix token.
traps: Adding softmax inside the model's training forward path. Return raw logits; the loss owns normalization.
Matching a CS336 snapshot with a tied output head. Its supplied embedding and lm_head weights are independent; test untied mode there and tying separately.
Checking causality only in the attention matrix. Cross-token normalization or a composition error can still alter prefix logits.

selfTest.q: Does tying the head remove the vocabulary projection's compute?
selfTest.a: No. It removes a separate VD weight matrix, but h @ E^T still costs about 2BTDV dense FLOPs.

selfTest.q: What should changing tokens after zero-based position i do to logits through i?
selfTest.a: Nothing within numerical tolerance, with identical prefix positions and deterministic evaluation. Those logits may depend on tokens at positions at most i, not the suffix.

selfTest.q: If sequence length doubles at fixed batch and width, which dominant terms quadruple?
selfTest.a: Dense QK and attention-times-V work, and the stored score/probability matrices, scale quadratically. Projection and FFN terms scale linearly with length.

selfTest.q: Why cannot an ordinary BERT forward pass serve as this causal decoder oracle?
selfTest.a: BERT uses bidirectional attention for masked-token prediction, so its representations can use right context. The decoder must preserve the causal prefix boundary.
